scores.evidence: Phase 1 "V1: Spike and load-test both conflict models" then "Hardened op-log schema (after V1 passes)"
scores.rationale: Mostly sound ordering (conflict model before schema/persistence), but auth is deferred to Phase 3 while persistence and external-style concerns precede it, and the Phase 0 stub uses last-write-wins before the model is proven; some inconsistencies (V3 placement, persistence gate in Phase 2 after Phase 1 built it).

scores.evidence: "One user opens a document in the editor → types a character → a second user ... sees it appear in <500ms"; deployed, behind flag, rollback tested
scores.rationale: Phase 0 is a real end-to-end deployed slice with logging and rollback, though in-memory and flag-gated.

scores.evidence: "Server-authoritative OT ... Flip Condition: Offline support required → flip to CRDT; if V1 shows OT bottleneck → flip to CRDT"
scores.rationale: Table lists irreversible decisions with reversibility class, default, assumption, validation and flip conditions, plus labeled budget assumptions.

scores.evidence: "Tasks (ordered by blast radius): 1. V1: Spike and load-test both conflict models"
scores.rationale: Conflict model first is widest-impact, but later phases (Phase 2 and 3 task lists) are not clearly ordered by blast radius, and auth hardening sits late.

scores.evidence: "Phase 0: Internal-only access (feature flag: email ends with @company.com); no external data; WebSocket auth stub (header check)."
scores.rationale: Security has an entry in every phase, but it is thin early and real auth/ACL and audit are late (Phase 3); also inconsistent between Phase 1 table and Phase 3 tasks.

scores.evidence: "Every request logged with timestamp, user (stub ID), document ID, operation, latency, outcome. One trace ID per user session"
scores.rationale: Concrete observability in Phase 0 and each later phase (metrics, tracing, SLA monitoring).

scores.evidence: "Docker image versioned by commit hash; deployment manifest in repo" ... "Staging environment mirrors production"
scores.rationale: Reproducibility has concrete treatment in each phase from Git/Docker through CI, staging parity, and backup/restore.

scores.evidence: "Graceful WebSocket close on error; client-side retry logic (not in Phase 0, but documented for Phase 2)."
scores.rationale: Resilience appears in each phase but Phase 0 is minimal and most substantive treatment (replicas, retries, failover) is in later phases.

scores.evidence: "N/A — no AI component in the request."
scores.rationale: Plan explicitly declares the AI layer N/A, despite a slightly hedging mention earlier.

scores.evidence: "Offline editing ... Pull-forward condition: customer requirement (Phase 3) or Phase 4 planning gates it"
scores.rationale: Explicit deferred list with rationale and pull-forward or revisit triggers for each item, though some triggers are vague.

note: Strong, well-structured plan with a real walking skeleton, tradeoff gates and threaded observability/reproducibility; weaknesses are late real auth, some ordering inconsistencies, and uneven blast-radius ordering.
